strategyPoints: Tire management will be crucial on this short, intense layout. Expect to see drivers pushing hard from start to finish.
With such a short lap, the pit window will be tight, so teams need to be precise with their strategy.
Fuel load is less of a concern on the short layout, allowing teams to run lighter and potentially gain an advantage.
The shortened track means more laps, increasing the chances of a safety car and throwing strategies into disarray.
Teams are closely monitoring the wear rate on the tires. Can they make a one-stop strategy work on this abrasive surface?
The undercut could be incredibly powerful on this short layout. A well-timed pit stop could gain several positions.
With fewer overtaking opportunities than the full layout, track position is paramount. A good start is essential.
The teams are looking at optimal strategies based on historical data, but the short layout means a lot of that data is useless. It's all about reacting to the race as it unfolds.
